body:
> In joint_3d_gizmo_plugin.cpp: node_body_a and node_body_b are dereferenced without checking whether Object::cast_to actually succeeded: Node3D *node_body_a = nullptr; if (!joint->get_node_a().is_empty()) { node_body_a = Object::cast_to(joint->get_node(joint->get_node_a())); Vector3 pos = node_body_a->get_global_position(); // Segfault if node_body_a is null If the NodePath is invalid (e.g. points to a deleted node, an invalid path, or a node that doesn't inherit from Node3D), get_node() or cast_to will return nullptr. Calling get_global_position() on it will immediately crash the editor. Wrapping the position lookup and redraw check inside an "if (node_body_a)" check (and similarly for node_body_b) should resolve this: if (!joint->get_node_a().is_empty()) { node_body_a = Object::cast_to(joint->get_node(joint->get_node_a())); if (node_body_a) { Vector3 pos = node_body_a->get_global_position(); Vector3 &prev_pos = it->value.node_a_last_global_pos; code Code if (!pos.is_equal_approx(prev_pos)) { prev_pos = pos; perform_redraw = true; } } } (Flagged by a local pre-push risk checker I've been developing: [https://github.com/Spacexcx/pr-check](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2FSpacexcx%2Fpr-check) , verified manually).

Thank you for this very human response. Fixed.
